task: Move checked-body encoding implementations out of a shared compiler header while preserving direct C++ controls.
observation: The H3 source-free and checked-body test scripts compile some C++ harnesses directly from one source file instead of using the common support-object list. Moving checked-body encoders out of line correctly exposed missing link dependencies in those harnesses; the first H3 run failed with undefined references to encode_checked_body_v1 and compute_checked_body_hash_v1, and the checked-body unit harness then exposed its dependency on Type::parse_canonical. Adding the implementation objects to both harness commands made the original assertions pass unchanged.
impact: Header implementation isolation is safe only when standalone C++ controls link the owning implementation units; this repository has a small number of intentional header-only harness commands that are easy to miss by source inspection.
evidence: python3 tests/tooling/check_phase25_h3_source_free_chain.py build/compiler/moss-dev initially failed to link check_phase25_h3_chain_records.cpp with undefined checked-body encoder/hash symbols
python3 tests/tooling/check_phase25_checked_body_ir.py build/compiler/moss-dev initially failed to link Type::parse_canonical after linking checked_body_ir.cpp only
Both focused scripts pass after linking checked_body_ir.cpp and type_ir.cpp as needed; their assertions were unchanged
tests/tooling/compiler_test_support.py supplies the production support objects to direct harnesses that use it

resolution.summary: Updated the two direct test commands to link the moved implementation owners and retained all existing checks.

tool_used: GNU C++ linker and repository Python C++ test harnesses
suggestion: When moving header bodies out of line, search and run all C++ harnesses that compile a single source directly, in addition to the common support-object test path.
